title: The canonical coefficient cone is limiting
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, A its valuation ring and varpi the recorded uniformizer. Let X be any scheme. Use the continuous coefficient sheaves, scalar maps, normalized towers and quotient predicate of [def-per-integral-lisse-reduction-data]. The cone from the continuous integral coefficient ring sheaf A_X to the positive finite continuous coefficient diagram, whose legs are pointwise quotient maps, is a limit cone of sheaves of commutative rings.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1), p. 59; the reduction ring identification is the rank-one reduction in this proposition.

proof.text: Use the normalized ring equivalence from the profinite integer tower. Its discrete coordinate projections are continuous. Since each ring quotient map has the quotient topology, the identity from the quotient topology to the discrete topology is continuous. Given compatible continuous quotient-valued functions, their pointwise values form an element of the compatible-family subring. Continuity into the discrete product follows coordinatewise, and the inverse homeomorphism gives a continuous integral-valued function. The normalization of the ring equivalence proves the projection identities and uniqueness pointwise. The forgetful functor from commutative rings reflects these limits because it preserves limits and reflects isomorphisms. Evaluation jointly reflects presheaf limits, and the sheaf inclusion reflects them. This proves the canonical cone limiting on any scheme, including empty objects.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Proposition 6.8.4(1), coefficient and local-basis arguments
